title: Machine Learning Model Evaluation & Drift Detection
description: A comprehensive reference course covering classification, regression, and ranking metrics, alongside Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) testing and Population Stability Index (PSI) drift monitoring in MLOps.
body: Maintain production machine learning reliability. Master offline model evaluation metrics, ranking metrics (NDCG, MAP), and automated statistical drift detection pipelines.

lessons.title: Lesson 1.1: Precision vs. Recall Trade-Offs & F1 Score
lessons.body:
### Cost Asymmetry in Machine Learning
Select evaluation metrics based on the business penalty of False Positives vs False Negatives:
- **Precision:** TP / (TP + FP) (Critical for spam filtering)
- **Recall:** TP / (TP + FN) (Critical for medical diagnosis & security threat detection)
- **F1 Score:** 2 * (Precision * Recall) / (Precision + Recall)

lessons.title: Lesson 1.2: Recommendation & Search Ranking Metrics (NDCG & MAP)
lessons.body:
### Measuring Result Position Ordering
Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG) penalizes highly relevant search items placed lower in recommendation lists.

sections.title: Section 2: Detecting Production Data Drift & Concept Drift

lessons.title: Lesson 2.1: Data Drift (Covariate Shift) vs. Concept Drift
lessons.body:
### The Shift Problem
- **Data Drift:** Input feature distribution P(X) changes while target relationship P(Y|X) remains static.
- **Concept Drift:** Relationship P(Y|X) shifts due to real-world behavioral changes.

lessons.title: Lesson 2.2: Python Implementation: Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) & PSI
lessons.body:
### Automated Monitoring Script

```python
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import ks_2samp

def detect_ks_drift(reference_data: np.ndarray, current_data: np.ndarray, threshold: float = 0.05) -> bool:
    statistic, p_value = ks_2samp(reference_data, current_data)
    return p_value < threshold
```
